notes.title: DevLog: when devs speak to players...
notes.content: [p]In Masters Of Gaia, your [b]followers[/b] will quickly try to protect themselves from harsh weather and other catastrophes that will befall them. They will thus begin to build shelters with the first elements they find nearby. [/p][p]But this is no ordinary city-builder. Here, the city doesn’t rise from blueprints and perfect planning—it grows organically, forged by the will of your people… and guided by your divine hand. You may choose to bless their efforts, beautify what they create, or tear down what dares to defy your vision. [/p][p]This is their world to build. But it is yours to shape. [/p][h2]Key Points[/h2][p]The creation of cities will be influenced by many parameters: [/p][h3][i]Technology [/i][/h3][p][b]Technology[/b] will allow for the construction of increasingly robust buildings, made of stone, glass, and other elaborate materials. Houses will be taller and able to accommodate more people, which is an advantage for avoiding excessive sprawl and preserving nature, something Gaia will appreciate! [/p][h3][i]Their Behavior[/i][/h3][p]Followers will have specific behaviors as well as common traits, which you can try to influence to some extent. Are your followers [b]orderly and conscientious[/b]? Then your cities will have straight streets with right-angle intersections, like the Romans. Or are they a little more [b]poetic and dreamlike[/b]? The streets will tend to twist and form beautiful curves. They might have more charm but be slightly less dense. Each style has its advantages and disadvantages; it's up to you to discover them! [/p][h3][i]Their Loyalty[/i][/h3][p]Your followers have their [b]free will[/b] and will sometimes make it clear! You will occasionally have to forbid them from building in a certain sacred area (for example, a forest that Gaia wants to preserve at all costs), but it's not guaranteed they'll always listen to you! You'll need to regularly monitor where they extend their city, and you might even have to destroy part of their creation. This could have a more or less lasting impact on your relationship with your followers. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/bd3cd9e71179eea2a52006ad7f4eb634bae686a7.png"][/img][/p][h2]From Humble Huts to Grand Cities [/h2][p]Your minions will start with miserable hovels. As they discover new technologies and gain access to better materials, they'll be able to build more comfortable and solid dwellings, capable of withstanding the worst weather or even an onslaught of bloodthirsty monsters. [/p][p]Our city system needs to be [b]evolutionary[/b]: street layouts will be maintained to some extent, and houses and other buildings will gradually improve. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/bd3cd9e71179eea2a52006ad7f4eb634bae686a7.png"][/img][/p][h2]Self-Building Cities[/h2][p]We had to design our own algorithms so that cities could [b]self-develop[/b] while maintaining a natural feel. [/p][p]Cities must be able to adapt to very different types of terrain. Of course, as in any God-like game, you'll be able to level the terrain (and your followers will also have a limited capacity), but we also wanted cities to be able to adapt to varied landscapes. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/b93271e3368df1278589412ca400a32beaaced59.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/1545e60d24acc413e1e3c92612141e5694a7ee0f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/eb2e737fc31e22e49dd3fc786a34f39ff958fee6.png"][/img][/p][h2]Configurable Cities [/h2][p]The various [b]decorative elements[/b] of the city can be configured. [/p][p]Depending on the technological levels, the types of buildings and decorations can change. City walls, houses, streets, decorative elements – everything can be precisely configured, and the city system must be able to spawn elements in the right place. [/p][p]Ultimately, it will be possible to [b]mod every element[/b] to create very different types of cities. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/747bb97bfd9fc6feb59218aa40a22d3135b9c1b4.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Making Masters of Gaia - Weekly sneak peek
notes.content: [p]In Masters of Gaia, your people are usually self-sufficient when it comes to food. They hunt, gather, farm, and adapt on their own.[/p][p]But when harsh climates hit, or Gaia throws a tantrum… that’s when a little divine assistance can change everything.[/p][p][/p][p]This god power lets you deliver food from the heavens ! A last-minute save, a reward for devotion, or just a show of mercy.[/p][p]Remember: you're not their babysitter. You're their god.[/p][p][/p][p]Would you use this power wisely… or throw apples just for fun?[/p][p][/p][p]We’ll be posting more updates like this as we build toward Early Access. And if you haven’t already — don’t forget to add Masters of Gaia to your wishlist! [/p][p][/p][p]Thanks for your support![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/c8103e80aa7d428850590eaea2b59db1dcc61efd.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: DevLog: when devs speak to players...
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/40edfac17d66f02a931fe10e1587f31ddcc6bb50.png[/img]

In Masters Of Gaia, your followers will face a diverse array of threats: from wandering [b]monsters[/b] and watchful [b]treasure guardians[/b] to [b]mystic creatures[/b], and even clashes with [b]other believers[/b]. 

As a God, you'll have the power to [u]guide and protect[/u] them through these trials – or perhaps choose a different path entirely. We're working diligently to deliver a unique and engaging experience as you navigate these divine choices. 

[h2]AI : tailored for our needs [/h2]
For the AI, we built [u]our own system in C++[/u] from scratch, allowing us to tailor it exactly to the needs of our game. It handles creature behavior both in the open world and during combat. 
The system is highly [u]configurable through Lua[/u] (we'll be speaking about Lua in Masters of Gaia very soon), making it easy for us to tweak and create a wide variety of behaviors for each creature. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/36e4ddd03bc60439a9f90e67c5272c99b1f40664.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/839991e7cd3247050beaaca87e650058c21e85a6.png[/img] 

[h2]Between human and ants [/h2]
Imagine a crowd somewhere between [u]individual humans[/u] and a bustling [u]ant colony[/u]. When danger looms, these believers are most likely to scatter and run! 

Given the hundreds populating our cities, we had to build AI systems that could [u]replicate large-scale crowd reactions[/u]. We envisioned their behavior as a blend of human reaction and the collective instinct of an ant hive. 

And you, the player, can shape this behavior. Through your efforts and magical powers, you can instill courage in them. However, a touch of randomness within each believer will always ensure unexpected encounters. Your ligntnings and fire bolts can help, too, but you will soon discover that damages can spread all across the battlefield... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/ca81402002e5ee73b046ed9d9daaf6402f1932a1.png[/img]

[h2]Battle avatar [/h2]
For the combat system, we needed to balance fights between one (or a few) monster(s) and a large group of believers, while ensuring players could meaningfully influence the outcome.  

We deliberately avoided managing massive armies. Not only because it’s a complex challenge and other games already excel at it, but more importantly, because hundreds of combatants could overwhelm players, making it hard to follow the action or react quickly. 

Instead, we focused on creating a [u]fresh, accessible approach to combat[/u] that keeps players engaged and in control. 

We opted for a turn-based-logic combat system (renderered in real-time) where a large crowd of believers can [u]channel their energies[/u] (life, capabilities, resistances) into a single fighter known as the [b]Battle Avatar[/b]. With the support of their allies, the Battle Avatar can [u]grow significantly stronger[/u] and stand a chance against the massive monsters that will eventually threaten your settlements. Think about the battle between Achilles fighting Hector, with his people around him, supporting and cheering. 

This powerful assistance comes at a price: [u]allies experience the battle[/u] as if they were fighting themselves, suffering damage whenever the Avatar does. They may even perish in combat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/9c85f1b3198ec7e8710fcd7adc641d06046b573d.png[/img]

[h2]It's your turn! [/h2]
While the combat system is turn-based, the world around you keeps moving. This means you’ll sometimes need to shift your focus to other tasks, even as battles continue to unfold. 

[u]You can support[/u] your believers with protective powers, disrupt the enemy using a different set of divine abilities, or simply do… nothing, letting your followers face their fate on their own. 

You can even choose to help the enemies, if that’s what you feel like doing. The choice is entirely yours. You'll discover that sometimes, a god's objectives can be beyond the immediate survival of a handful of creatures... 

The outcome of battles, along with the support you provide (or don’t), can significantly impact your believers. Those who become avatars, in particular, [u]may gain substantial[/u] experience and honor. Additionally, your actions during combat can [u]influence the trust[/u] that your believers have in you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45584859/156e44aa0464812f61800a05784d8e29e288625c.png[/img]

We hope you'll like this combat system. Feel free to [u]let us know[/u] what you think ! And follow us to get updates on the game development.

notes.title: Making Masters of Gaia - Weekly sneak peek
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We’re happy to share with you a quick behind-the-scenes look at something we’ve been building lately: combat in Masters of Gaia.

We imagined something interesting for the combat that will create fun strategical patterns. When danger appears — whether it's a wild beast or a pair of angry giant spiders — the most appropriate character is selected to face the threat. But he might not be alone.

Behind him, additional supporters channel their energy, empowering the defender with collective strength. Think of it like a spiritual support system: the more believers around, the stronger your frontline champion becomes.

This system lets us create dynamic fights where the quality of faith and positioning matters more than brute numbers.

We’re still tuning the visuals and balance, but it's already really fun to test ! Here are a few early screenshots showing this in action. Let us know what you think!

We’ll be posting more updates like this as we build toward Early Access. And if you haven’t already — don’t forget to add Masters of Gaia to your wishlist! 

Thanks for your support!
